ai.description: Tyson’s Leaping Frog reaches 35–45 mm. It is brown with dark lateral bands and a pale mid-dorsal stripe. Distinctive features include a pointed snout and elongated, slender limbs adapted for leaping.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Indirana tysoni* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-colored lateral band that extends from the snout through the eye to the shoulder.
ai.habitat: *Indirana tysoni* inhabits the leaf litter of primary evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Tyson's Leaping Frog is primarily nocturnal, exhibiting remarkable agility as it leaps across mossy rocks and vegetation near fast-flowing streams to hunt for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indirana tysoni* breeds during the monsoon season, laying small clutches of terrestrial eggs on mossy rocks near streams, which develop into semi-terrestrial tadpoles.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Indirana tysoni* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically restricted to high-elevation evergreen forests in the state of Kerala.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Indirana tysoni* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic chirps emitted from rocky, fast-flowing stream habitats.
